column1: # suite-floors.tsv — the minimum number of cases each suite must ACCOUNT FOR.
# Enforced by run-all.sh as:
#     assertions_made + cases_explicitly_skipped  >=  floor
# === Why a floor, when the suites already report pass/fail ===
# A suite that silently stops running half its cases still exits 0. It prints
# fewer PASS lines, the runner prints "ok", and the only trace is a number
# nobody has a reason to compare against anything. Every other check in this
# repository is about that shape; this is the same check pointed at the suites
# themselves.
# It is not hypothetical here. Before this file existed, one suite reported 44
# cases on two platforms and 25 on the third, in a fully green run, because a
# GNU-only `sed` construct emitted nothing under BSD sed. Nineteen assertions
# disappeared and every signal stayed green.
# === Why `+ skipped`, and why a bare SKIP counts as exactly ONE ===
# A case that genuinely cannot run on a platform — no cygpath, no python-free
# PATH, not a drive-form path — is legitimate. It just has to SAY so. Counting
# skips keeps such a suite passing while making the skip visible.
# The counting rule is what stops that being a loophole: one SKIP line counts as
# one case. A block-level skip standing in for three assertions therefore fails
# the floor, and the fix is to emit one SKIP per skipped case — which is also the
# honest thing to print. Coverage that moves platform to platform should be
# legible, not summarised.
# === These numbers are MEASURED, not estimated ===
# Each is the observed `assertions + skips` from a full run. Raise one only after
# adding cases and re-measuring. Lowering one is a coverage decision and wants a
# sentence in the commit message saying which cases went and why.
# Format: <suite filename><TAB><floor>
